summary: The bill requires federal judges to add consecutive prison terms of 10, 15, or life years to sentences for defendants who accumulate three strikes from listed federal and state misdemeanors and felonies, with strikes weighted by offense type and reduced for juvenile convictions.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends federal criminal sentencing statutes to impose enhanced penalties on repeat offenders. It contains no provisions related to appropriations, budgets, or government expenditures.
The bill addresses only criminal sentencing enhancements and contains no tax-related provisions.
The bill makes no reference to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.

Numerous federal and state firearm offenses are listed as strike-eligible felonies that trigger enhanced sentences. This strengthens enforcement of existing gun laws against repeat offenders but does not enact new ownership restrictions or expand gun rights.

Certain immigration offenses (8 U.S.C. §§ 1324 and 1328) are included among strike-eligible crimes, resulting in harsher penalties for repeat violators. This has a tangential effect favoring stricter enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending or policy.
The bill has no environmental or regulatory provisions.
No provisions affect welfare programs or social safety-net benefits.
The bill does not address education policy or funding.

Multiple Controlled Substances Act violations and state drug-trafficking offenses are defined as strike-eligible, triggering mandatory sentencing enhancements for repeat offenders. This directly advances stricter drug enforcement.

The entire bill establishes a federal three-strikes sentencing regime that adds consecutive terms of 10 years, 15 years, or life imprisonment for qualifying repeat offenders. This is a core tough-on-crime measure focused exclusively on enhanced sentencing.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill has no fiscal or deficit-related content.
The bill contains no provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No foreign-aid provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address voting rights or election procedures.
No technology, data-privacy, or regulatory provisions are included.
The bill has no labor or union-related content.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
